title: One new rule per level
description: A proposed cumulative word course for the Reading Learner app. Each small level adds one focus; earlier patterns can appear again.
scope: Reviewable curriculum map only. The running app still uses its existing ten word levels.
prerequisitesNote: The sequence is cumulative: every level assumes the patterns from all earlier levels. Listed prerequisites highlight additional earlier patterns inside its focus words; they are not a separate route through the course.
startingSkills: The child recognises the ordinary single-letter consonant sounds, including hard c and g, consonant y, and x as ks.
The child can attempt blending simple consonant-vowel-consonant words.
These are provisional assumptions, not confirmed assessment results. Check them before adopting the course.
startingWordsNote: Use these only if the child already reads them independently. Choose and confirm the familiar starter bank before the first practice round. Do not label an unseen word an easy win merely because it is decodable.

roundRecipe.opening: Three familiar words, drawn from the child's demonstrated known-word bank.
roundRecipe.focus: Four encounters from the current level's focus bank. Rotate the bank across rounds; the whole level need not fit in one round.
roundRecipe.closing: Three familiar words again. Repeats of known words are allowed.
roundRecipe.reviewSelection: The lists below are candidates. Use a candidate only after the child has demonstrated it is familiar. Earlier levels remain available for review; there is no requirement to use every candidate.
roundRecipe.noKnownWords: Confirm starting skills and a familiar starter bank before enabling this course. If the prerequisite is not met, address the foundation explicitly rather than presenting unfamiliar words as wins.

completion.description: Only the focus bank determines level completion. Keep the current requirement of two qualifying first-attempt Yes confirmations per focus word. A helped repeat advances the encounter but does not earn a qualifying first-attempt Yes.
completion.familiarWords: Opening and closing words do not add new completion requirements.
completion.earnedProgress: Preserve existing word trophies and earned confirmations. An already mastered focus word keeps its credit.
completion.restart: Start the new course at the first unfinished focus bank using preserved word progress. Let a parent choose Level 1 for practice without wiping trophies.
completion.selfCheck: Keep the current record → expected word → Got it? → Yes or record again flow. The voice-recognition experiment is not part of this proposal.
completion.ruleChips: Show the current level's one focus as the primary rule chip. Earlier spelling help remains available through the word's sound buttons; do not automatically introduce extra rule chips in a focused round.

deferredPatterns.reason: Separate spelling cohorts need their own levels; ee and ea should not share a new-rule level.

deferredPatterns.pattern: u-e saying oo and coalescing sounds
deferredPatterns.reason: Keep them separate from the yoo cohort.
baby combines an open syllable, final y and more than one syllable.

deferredPatterns.pattern: Soft c and g, ph and wh
deferredPatterns.reason: Introduce each pattern separately after the core course.

deferredPatterns.pattern: Silent consonants and further consonant teams
deferredPatterns.reason: They are additional correspondences, outside this first map.
music and longer words require more than the core single-syllable patterns.
Words such as the, of, was and have need deliberate separate teaching. Teaching quiet th and buzzy th does not cover the exceptional vowel in the.
live and similar words need context or an explicitly selected meaning before they are suitable focus items.

implementationNotes.before: A word's single numeric level drives both selection and completion.
implementationNotes.after: Give the new word course explicit focus banks and review membership; keep one stable progress record per word.
implementationNotes.reason: The same familiar word can support many later levels without gaining new mastery requirements.

implementationNotes.before: Missing canonical words are deleted from stored progress during loading.
implementationNotes.after: Keep all existing word identities in the catalog, including parked words; only remove them from this course's selection.
implementationNotes.reason: Deferred words must retain their trophies, attempts and settings.

implementationNotes.before: The old course's numeric level and old one-time migrations describe the ten-level sequence.
implementationNotes.after: Introduce a new word-course identity and an explicit migration; preserve old history and select the first unfinished focus bank.
implementationNotes.reason: Old Level 3 cannot silently acquire the meaning of the new Level 3.

implementationNotes.before: Word and number practice share MAX_LEVEL = 10.
implementationNotes.after: Use independent word-course and number-course bounds.
implementationNotes.reason: The proposed 41 word levels do not change the ten number levels.

implementationNotes.before: Artwork is assigned only to the ten old word levels.
implementationNotes.after: Use the explicit41-picture assignments recorded in this course, retaining source and licence credits for the real tank photographs.
implementationNotes.reason: Every proposed word level has a different, deliberate image assignment.

implementationNotes.before: Sound buttons and family tags cover the existing vocabulary.
implementationNotes.after: Audit the segmentation, sound clips and rule wording for every proposed focus word before adoption; add needed word-specific sound definitions.
implementationNotes.reason: A valid spelling bank can still play the wrong sound through an old override.

implementationNotes.before: Rules heard flags and recap selection rely on old rule IDs and numeric levels.
implementationNotes.after: Scope rule introductions to the new focus sequence and select word recaps by course membership; ensure number items cannot enter word recaps.
implementationNotes.reason: Previously heard rules and old numeric levels must not suppress or misdirect the new course.

implementationNotes.before: Several existing rule tags are inconsistent, including both, shall, water and music.
implementationNotes.after: The current app now corrects those four annotations and demonstrates rules with recorded sounds and whole-word examples. Audit every new bank before course adoption.
implementationNotes.reason: Those known errors have been fixed; the new vocabulary still needs a complete pronunciation audit.

sources.title: Department for Education: choosing a phonics teaching programme
sources.purpose: Supports using a systematic progression. This custom map is not a DfE-validated programme.

sources.title: Letters and Sounds
sources.purpose: A phonics reference for correspondences and blending, not an endorsement of this custom word order.

reviewNotes: One new focus means one unfamiliar spelling pattern or blending skill. A word may use several earlier patterns.
Every candidate still needs a child's-eye check for pronunciation and meaning. The word lists do not certify teaching quality.
The focus labels describe these word cohorts, not universal rules for every English word.
Review the starting assumptions and the first five banks before adopting the proposed course. No extra reference-audio recordings are required.
rulePlaybackNote: Each letter name is spoken slowly on its own, with a short pause. The lesson then demonstrates the recorded phonics sound and whole-word examples. The U-name demonstration uses the real word you. Blending lessons play the separate consonant sounds before the whole word.
artworkNote: Every planned word level has its own picture: ten existing space-knight pictures at milestones, with 31 real tank photographs between them. Photo credits are listed below. These pictures are ready for the proposed 41-level course; the app currently uses its ten-level course.
